messages.cli.doctor.adapter_doctor_failed: Tribe {tribe}: the adapter file cannot find or run its CLI: {detail}
messages.cli.doctor.adapter_file_broken: Tribe {tribe}: the adapter file {adapter} does not load, or what it builds does not keep the contract:
messages.cli.doctor.acknowledge_disabled: --acknowledge-terms {tribe}: tribe {tribe} is disabled, so doctor skips it and would record nothing. Enable it in the same command: elvaria doctor --enable {tribe} --acknowledge-terms {tribe}
messages.cli.doctor.auth_not_declared: Tribe {tribe}: adapter {adapter} runs with {declared}, not {auth}. Set tribes[].tool.auth in kingdom.json to one of them.
messages.cli.doctor.account_same_account: Tribe {tribe}: its CLI is signed in to the same account as tribe {other}'s, in another config folder, so both tribes would spend one account's mana. Sign in to another account in one of the two folders.
messages.cli.doctor.account_same_default: Tribe {tribe}: like tribe {other}, it names no config folder, so both run {adapter} in the CLI's default folder and spend one account's mana. Give one of them a folder of its own and sign in there once: elvaria doctor --config-dir <tribe>=<folder>.
messages.cli.doctor.account_same_dir: Tribe {tribe}: its CLI runs in the same config folder as tribe {other}'s ({path}), so both tribes would spend one account's mana. Give one of them a folder of its own and sign in there once: elvaria doctor --config-dir <tribe>=<folder>.
messages.cli.doctor.bad_config_dir_option: --config-dir takes <tribe>=<folder>, e.g. claude_2=C:/Users/you/.elvaria/accounts/claude_2; an empty folder (claude_2=) removes it.
messages.cli.doctor.command_shell_syntax: Territory {id}: these commands hold shell syntax (a pipe, &&, $VAR, a redirection, an unclosed quote); the Steward runs commands without a shell, so they cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.config_dir_in_kingdom: Tribe {tribe}: the config folder {path} lies inside the kingdom ({folder}). It holds the account's sign-in and every transcript, and the characters' tools reach the kingdom: keep it outside, e.g. ~/.elvaria/accounts/{tribe}.
messages.cli.doctor.config_dir_in_territory: Tribe {tribe}: the config folder {path} lies inside territory {territory} ({folder}). It holds the account's sign-in and every transcript, and the characters' tools reach a territory: keep it outside, e.g. ~/.elvaria/accounts/{tribe}.
messages.cli.doctor.config_dir_missing: --config-dir {tribe}={path}: no such folder. Create it, sign in to the tribe's CLI there once (docs/guides/adding-a-tribe.md), then run doctor again.
messages.cli.doctor.config_dir_not_declared: Tribe {tribe}: kingdom.json names a config folder ({path}), but adapter {adapter} does not run its CLI in one, so every session would use the CLI's default account. Remove it (elvaria doctor --config-dir {tribe}=) or use an adapter that declares config_dir.
messages.cli.doctor.sibling.look_ignored: Sibling {tribe} has a look in kingdom.json, but a sibling wears the look of tribe {root}, so that look is ignored. Remove it; name the sibling with elvaria tribe look {tribe} --name, and change the parts with elvaria tribe look {root}.
messages.cli.doctor.sibling.no_root: Tribe {tribe} has sibling_of {root}, but the kingdom has no tribe {root}: {tribe} looks as a tribe of its own. Set sibling_of in kingdom.json to the id of its root, or remove it.
messages.cli.doctor.sibling.other_adapter: Sibling {tribe} runs adapter {adapter}, while its root {root} runs adapter {root_adapter}: a sibling is a second account of the same CLI. If {tribe} is a tribe of its own, remove its sibling_of from kingdom.json.
messages.cli.doctor.sibling.own_root: Tribe {tribe} has a sibling_of that names itself: it looks as a tribe of its own. Point sibling_of at its root in kingdom.json, or remove it.
messages.cli.doctor.sibling.root_is_sibling: Tribe {tribe} has sibling_of {root}, and {root} is a sibling itself: a sibling is no root, so {tribe} looks as a tribe of its own. Point the sibling_of of {tribe} at the root of {root}.
messages.cli.doctor.config_dir_relative: --config-dir {tribe}={path}: the folder must be an absolute path.
messages.cli.doctor.enable_adapter_file: --enable {tribe}: the adapter of tribe {tribe} is a file of yours ({adapter}) that has passed no conformance suite yet. Run elvaria tribe check {tribe}: it runs the suite and enables the tribe once it passes.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_down: Docker is not running (docker info does not answer) and territories {ids} have commands that use docker: open Docker Desktop (or start the daemon) before elvaria run. With Docker off, resets and e2e checks fail on the environment: the Steward opens no judge and demotes nobody, but runs them again every {minutes} minutes until Docker is up.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_missing: The docker program is not on PATH, and territories {ids} have commands that use docker.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_up: Docker is running (server {version}); territories {ids} have commands that use docker.
messages.cli.doctor.git_identity_hint: Set one: git -C "{path}" config user.name "<name>" and git -C "{path}" config user.email "<email>" (add --global for every repo).
messages.cli.doctor.git_identity_missing: Territory {id}: git has no user.email in the repo {path}, so the Steward's commits (the submit, a half-done piece kept) will fail and the quest goes to the infirmary with the commit trip.
messages.cli.doctor.git_missing: git was not found on PATH.
messages.cli.doctor.git_merge_tree: git {version} is older than {min}: the merge queue cannot try a merge with git merge-tree, so the deliveries of {territories} (which name shared_paths) will stop at the update. Update git.
messages.cli.doctor.one_pool_judges: Doers on the model {model} have judges of another model on one mana pool only (pool {pool} of tribe {tribe}: {judges}): when that pool closes, or they are suspended, work from that model has nobody to judge it. Add a judge of another model on another mana pool, best on another account.
messages.cli.doctor.login_failed: its adapter says the CLI cannot sign in, without saying why.
messages.cli.doctor.note.bad_note: the adapter file returned a note with an unknown code or wrong parameters ({code}).
messages.cli.doctor.note.command_timed_out: {command} did not answer within {seconds} s and was stopped (a busy machine or a slow network): try again.
messages.cli.doctor.note.config_dir_ignored: the CLI runs in the config folder {used}, not in {given} as the tribe names: it did not take the folder, so every session would use another account.
messages.cli.doctor.note.hook_missing: the Elvaria hook is not built, {file} is missing: run pnpm --filter @elvaria/hooks build.
messages.cli.doctor.note.not_signed_in: {command} shows it is not signed in (or offline): sign in with {login}.
messages.cli.doctor.note.sign_in_ending: the sign-in ends by {date}: run {login} before then.
messages.cli.doctor.note.terms_not_acknowledged: the owner has not acknowledged the provider's terms (ADR 0018): elvaria doctor --acknowledge-terms.
messages.cli.doctor.option.acknowledge: Record that you have read and accept the provider's terms for this tribe (ADR 0018).
messages.cli.doctor.option.config_dir: The config folder of a tribe's CLI, where it keeps its sign-in, e.g. claude_2=C:/Users/you/.elvaria/accounts/claude_2: sign in to the CLI there once, and the tribe runs on that account. An empty folder (claude_2=) removes it; repeat for several tribes.
messages.cli.doctor.option.enable: Check a disabled tribe like every enabled one and turn it on in kingdom.json (enabled: true) only when nothing is wrong with it. A tribe whose adapter is a file of yours is enabled by elvaria tribe check instead.
messages.cli.doctor.option.pin: Pin the CLI version and path just found when they differ from the pinned ones, for every such tribe. It checks nothing: the Steward holds a tribe until elvaria tribe check passes on its new version, and that command pins one tribe once it passes.
messages.cli.doctor.option.tool: Path to a tribe's CLI when it is not on PATH, e.g. claude=C:/…/claude.exe; repeat for several tribes.
messages.cli.doctor.pin_hint: Read the CLI's changelog, then: elvaria tribe check {tribe} (the real CLI, a few short sessions, a little mana). Once it passes it pins the version it ran, for this tribe alone, and the tribe works again.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell runs local scripts (Execution Policy {policy}), so pnpm.ps1 and npm's other shims start in its sessions.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_hint: In PowerShell run: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned (local scripts run, downloaded ones need a signature). A policy set by Group Policy is for the machine's admin to change.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_missing: Tribe {tribe}: powershell.exe was not found on PATH, so whether it runs scripts (pnpm.ps1) was not checked.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_refuses: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell refuses scripts (Execution Policy {policy}). Its sessions run commands in powershell.exe, where pnpm is pnpm.ps1: every pnpm command fails, and a judge cannot run the tests it should try.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_unread: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell did not say its Execution Policy (Get-ExecutionPolicy), so whether it runs scripts (pnpm.ps1) was not checked.
messages.cli.doctor.program_hint: doctor looks on the PATH of the shell it runs in, as elvaria run does: add the program's folder to PATH where elvaria run starts (Git for Windows keeps sh in C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin), or change the command.
messages.cli.doctor.program_missing: Territory {id}: {program} is not on PATH, so these commands cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.program_shell_only: Territory {id}: {program} is {path}, which only a shell can start (a .cmd or .bat that does not run a Node script), so these commands cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.prompt_max: Tribe {tribe}: its CLI takes a user prompt of at most {max} characters on this machine; the Steward passes over a judge of this tribe whose review prompt is longer.
messages.cli.doctor.vision: Tribe {tribe}: its CLI reads images; its judges may take a quest whose ritual compares screens (visual_review).
messages.cli.doctor.programs: Territory {id}: the programs of its {count} commands are on PATH ({programs}).
messages.cli.doctor.registry: Registry: {kinds} quest kinds, {classes} classes, {rituals} rituals, {scripts} scripts, {tags} tags.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_behind: The registry lacks {count} entries or fields this Elvaria ships (they came after the kingdom was made):
messages.cli.doctor.registry_behind_hint: elvaria migrate adds the missing entries whole and leaves every entry you have as it is; copy a missing field from {path} by hand if you want it.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_missing: The registry names {count} catalog scripts the kingdom does not have:
messages.cli.doctor.seal_kinds_unknown: kingdom.delegation.seal.kinds names kinds the registry lacks: {kinds}; quests of those kinds are never spared the seal.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_prompts_hint: Run elvaria migrate: it copies the missing class prompts from {path} into registry/prompts/ and leaves the ones you have.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_files_hint: Run elvaria migrate: it copies the registry files this Elvaria ships and the kingdom lacks from {path}, and leaves the ones you have.
messages.cli.doctor.rules_outside_patch: Territory {id}: {count} files under .claude/rules are not in laws.patch_paths; Claude Code cannot write them, so a character has to ask the owner instead of editing. Add "{glob}" to laws.patch_paths in territories/{id}/territory.json:
messages.cli.doctor.rules_patchable: Territory {id}: the {count} files under .claude/rules are all in laws.patch_paths.
messages.cli.doctor.claude_local: Territory {id}: the repo has a CLAUDE.local.md, and Claude Code loads it into every plot under {dir} (it sits in a parent folder), so characters read your personal notes. Move it out of the repo.
messages.cli.doctor.saved: Wrote the tool of tribe {tribes} into kingdom.json.
messages.cli.doctor.shell: Tribe {tribe}: its sessions run commands in {shell}.
messages.cli.doctor.summary: Check that this machine is ready: registry, git, each tribe's CLI (and on Windows whether PowerShell runs scripts, for a tribe whose sessions run commands in it), the territories and the programs their commands start, the treasury, sessions left running.
messages.cli.doctor.terms_refused: Tribe {tribe}: Antigravity's terms are not acknowledged, so this tribe does not run yet (ADR 0018).
messages.cli.doctor.territory_not_git: Territory {id}: {path} is no longer a git repo.
messages.cli.doctor.territory_unchecked: Territory {id}: {path}; its repo cannot be checked without git.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_changed: Tribe {tribe}: the CLI at {path} updated itself from {pinned} to {version}. The Steward opens no new session for the tribe until a check with the real CLI passes on {version}.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_unchecked: Tribe {tribe}: version {version} is pinned, but no check with the real CLI passed on it (the last one passed on {checked}); the Steward opens no new session for the tribe until one does.
messages.cli.doctor.held_in_trial: Tribe {tribe} is held (its CLI changed version or is gone): in the trial of elvaria upgrade its errors are only warnings, since the new build's Steward opens no session for it until elvaria tribe check {tribe} passes.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_hint: Show doctor the way: elvaria doctor --tool {tribe}=<path to the CLI>
messages.cli.doctor.tool_moved: Tribe {tribe}: the pinned {pinned_path} is gone; found {path}, version {version}. The tribe cannot run, and the Steward opens no new session for it, until a check with the real CLI pins the one found.
messages.cli.doctor.moved_hint: Read the CLI's changelog, then: elvaria tribe check {tribe} (it tries the CLI just found, a few short sessions, a little mana). Once it passes it pins that CLI, path and version, for this tribe alone; then restart elvaria run if it runs.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_missing: Tribe {tribe}: {program} was not found on PATH.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_path_bad: Tribe {tribe}: the path given to --tool is not a file ({program}).
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_enabled: Tribe {tribe} is now enabled in kingdom.json.
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_still_disabled: Tribe {tribe} stays disabled until the problem above is fixed.
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_invalid: Tribe {tribe}: its settings are not valid once the tool is filled in:
messages.cli.doctor.unknown_adapter: Tribe {tribe}: there is no built-in adapter {adapter}; a tribe names a built-in adapter or an adapter file adapters/<name>.mjs.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury: Treasury {path}: {count} names, every name the territories allow.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_absent: Treasury {path}: no file yet; no territory allows a secret.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_acl_shared: Treasury {path}: other accounts have read access: {accounts}.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_acl_fix: Open Properties > Security > Advanced for {path}. Disable inheritance (convert inherited permissions), then remove read access for the listed accounts; retain the current user, SYSTEM and Administrators. Run elvaria doctor again.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_acl_unreadable: Treasury {path}: cannot inspect Windows ACL ({reason}). Check access to the file and that Windows icacls and whoami are available, then run elvaria doctor again.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_missing_names: Treasury {path} lacks names the territories allow; a quest asking for one goes to the infirmary:
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_shared: Treasury {path}: other users can read it (mode {mode}); the Steward opens no session that needs a secret. Run: chmod 600 "{path}"
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_not_object: Treasury {path} is not a JSON object of the form { "name": "value" }.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_bad_name: Treasury {path}: "{name}" is not a secret name (snake_case, like npm_token).
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_bad_value: Treasury {path}: the value of {name} is not a non-empty string.
messages.cli.doctor.sessions_left: {count} sessions a stopped Steward left behind are still running; the next elvaria run kills them:
messages.cli.doctor.session_left_unknown: {quest}: {character} ({role}), pid {pid}: its start time is unknown, so elvaria run leaves it alone; check it by hand and stop it if it is this session
messages.cli.doctor.scripture_issues: Scripture: {errors} errors, {warnings} warnings; see elvaria scripture lint.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_unpinned: graphify is not pinned: run elvaria doctor --pin, or no quest gets a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_changed: graphify changed from {pinned} to {version}: check it, then run elvaria doctor --pin.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_no_version: graphify at {path} did not say its version; quests run without a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_missing: graphify not found: territories {territories} run their quests without a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_install: Install it with: uv tool install graphifyy (Python 3.10–3.14), then run elvaria doctor --pin.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_no_repo: Territory {id} delivers by {mode}, but its remote «{remote}» names no repo on {forge}: nothing can be pushed.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_no_git: Territory {id} delivers by {mode}, but git does not run there (no git, or the folder is gone), so no credential for {host} can be read.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_no_credential: Territory {id} delivers by {mode}, but git has no credential for {host}: the Steward could not push to {repo}.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_sign_in: Sign in once from a terminal: push any branch to {host} by hand and let git keep the credential (Git Credential Manager on Windows, the Keychain on macOS), then run elvaria doctor again.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_timeout: Territory {id}: git gave no credential for {host} within {seconds} s and was stopped.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_keychain: macOS asks once whether git may read the Keychain, in a window a background run never shows: run git credential fill once in a terminal (type protocol=https, host={host}, then an empty line) and choose Always Allow.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_slow: A busy machine, or a credential helper waiting on a window nobody sees: try again; if it stays, run git credential fill once in a terminal (protocol=https, host={host}, then an empty line).
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_credential: Territory {id} ({mode}): git has a credential for {host}.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_can_push: Territory {id}: {host} lets that account push to {repo}.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_read_only: Territory {id}: that account can read {repo} on {host} but not push to it: the Steward could not deliver there.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_refused: Territory {id}: {host} refused the credential for {repo} (HTTP {status}): sign in again, or allow the token for this organisation.
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_not_found: Territory {id}: {host} shows that account no repo {repo} (missing, or private to others).
messages.cli.doctor.delivery_unreachable: Territory {id}: could not ask {host} about {repo} ({detail}); the credential is there, run elvaria doctor again later.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_none: Territory {id} was never tried: run elvaria territory check {id} before its first quest.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_unreadable: The last trial of territory {id} cannot be read ({file}); run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_failed: Territory {id} failed its trial at {at}; fix it, then run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_stale: Territory {id}'s commands.setup or checks changed since its trial at {at}; run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_passed_gaps: Territory {id}: passed its trial at {at}; {count} other items of its scorecard do not pass.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_rerun: Why an item of the trial fails: elvaria territory check {id} (it tries the territory again).
